task_instance: Applied a firm KYC/AML rules grid to a sample corporate onboarding record (Meridian Trading Partners LLC, Cyprus, with a 2-layer BVI ownership structure) plus a sample screening-results file, to produce a risk rating, required-document check, cited rule-by-rule outcomes, and a final disposition JSON, per the skill's Step 1-4.
evidence: Created onboarding_record.json (structured applicant record analogous to kyc-doc-parse output), rules_grid.json (firm rules grid with high-risk jurisdiction list, per-applicant-type/rating document requirements, and 8 cited rules), and screening_results.json (a sample sanctions/PEP/adverse-media screening export, standing in for the screening MCP's output as a plain data file, since the runtime cannot call MCP tools). Manually applied every rule in the grid to the record: jurisdiction rule 1.1 and ownership-opacity rule 1.2 both fired (Cyprus applicant + BVI holding layer + 2-tier ownership), PEP rules 2.1/2.2/4.2 fired because screening confirmed UBO Radu Popescu as a PEP despite pep_declared=false on the record, sanctions/adverse-media rules 3.1/3.2 were n/a (no hits), and source-of-funds rule 4.1 passed (supported by sale_agreement_2022). Computed required documents for corporate/high rating from the grid and checked them against documents_received, finding proof_of_registered_address and ubo_declaration_form missing. Wrote the full result to kyc_assessment_result.json containing the risk factor table, risk_rating ('high'), required_document_check, a rule_outcomes array with every rule cited by id/text/outcome/evidence, and a final disposition block ('escalate-EDD', missing_documents, escalation_reasons) matching the schema in the skill's Step 4. Verified the deliverable by reading kyc_assessment_result.json back and confirming it is well-formed JSON with all required fields populated and internally consistent (disposition correctly withheld from 'clear' because rating is high, docs are missing, and escalation rules fired -- matching the skill's stated disposition logic that this skill never approves, only routes). All work used only Read/Write on text/JSON files in the work directory; no shell, no code execution, no MCP/connector tools, and no binary files were needed or used.
note: The only deviation from a literal reading of the skill is that 'screening results from the screening MCP' were supplied as a plain provided file instead of a live MCP call, since MCP tool use is forbidden in this runtime; the rules grid explicitly allows a provided-file alternative, and the same substitution is a reasonable, realistic proxy for screening results too (e.g. an exported screening report). This did not block the core deliverable: producing a risk rating, document check, cited rule outcomes, and disposition from structured inputs is pure text/JSON reasoning and was fully completed and verified.
